answer: Shale-deep duplicate burn: when a duplicate cluster is proven, each fake is burned in proportion to the depth of its attestation history — the older the clone, the more shale layers it must strip, so sunk cost grows with the clone's age. Every identity must first grow a reef of attested work before it may hold stake, so each anchor of stake in the pool is backed by real activity. A flash clone has no reef yet, holds no stake to defend, and burns cheap; a long-lived clone has built depth, and burning it costs the attacker its accumulated value.
